patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — PrestaShop and Shopify share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose PrestaShop only if your buying job matches “Open-source PHP commerce — Classic free; Hosted from ~$26/mo annual (€24 excl. VAT) with 1” rather than Shopify's shape. Choose Shopify only if your buying job matches “Hosted SaaS ecommerce platform with themes, checkout, channels, and POS — Basic from $39/m” rather than PrestaShop's shape. Workflow advantage: PrestaShop leans shared coverage; Shopify leans checkout-conversion, omnichannel-retail. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — PrestaShop and Shopify share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: PrestaShop is Open-source PHP commerce — Classic free; Hosted from ~$26/mo annual (€24 excl. VAT) with 14-day trial; Enterprise quote. WooCommerce keeps t; Shopify is Hosted SaaS ecommerce platform with themes, checkout, channels, and POS — Basic from $39/mo ($29 annual), Grow $105 ($79 annual), Advanced $.
- Company-size focus: PrestaShop (small-business, mid-market) vs Shopify (solo, micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: PrestaShop-leaning — vs Shopify-leaning checkout-conversion, omnichannel-retail.
- Researched limits: PrestaShop — Classic TCO (hosting, modules, agency) is not $0 even when the license is free; Shopify — Subscription plus apps/themes and payment spreads raise TCO versus headline plan price.

Limitations — PrestaShop: Classic TCO (hosting, modules, agency) is not $0 even when the license is free; POS / omnichannel is module-dependent, not a native retail bundle; Shopify: Subscription plus apps/themes and payment spreads raise TCO versus headline plan price; Third-party payment gateways incur additional transaction fees on lower tiers.

Poor-fit cases: PrestaShop is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Classic TCO (hosting, modules, agency) is not $0 even when the license is free · Shopify is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Subscription plus apps/themes and payment spreads raise TCO versus headline plan price · Avoid PrestaShop if you actually need Shopify's motion (Hosted SaaS ecommerce platform with themes, checkout, channels, and POS — Basic )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
